buckets.label: R — refusal
buckets.hint: Shouldn't be in an agent's hands at all

buckets.label: Rung 1 — draft only
buckets.hint: The agent drafts; a human does everything else

buckets.label: Rung 2 — propose, approve
buckets.hint: The agent stages; a human's click is the boundary

buckets.label: Rung 3 — act, audit trail
buckets.hint: The agent acts; the record shows everything

tasks.text: Extract a theme table from this quarter's survey verbatims
tasks.reasoning: Read-only input, structured checkable output, trivially reversible (regenerate), and your M3 checkpoint still reviews the artifact downstream. This is what rung 3 was made for. One caveat from Lesson 2: if the table were ranked by severity to direct investigation resources, the laundering test applies and the ranking step is person-adjacent even though extraction isn't.

tasks.text: Draft rejection emails for the week's declined candidates
tasks.reasoning: Rung 1, permanent. Drafting is legitimate, M1's sorting said so; anything above draft-only walks toward the person-line. The draft lands in a human's hands; a human sends, every time. The trap in the wording: 'draft' was always the rung: the question is refusing the climb.

tasks.text: Save the formatted debrief into the hiring channel's shared folder
tasks.reasoning: First rigged item. It feels routine and it's probably reversible, but 'save to where the hiring team reads' is a small publish. Rung 2 until the approval log shows you never decline; then rung 3 is an evidence-based conversation.

tasks.text: Send the weekly HR newsletter to the all-staff list
tasks.reasoning: The reverse trap: low stakes, so rung 3 feels fine, but send-to-all-staff is irreversible, and reversibility, not stakes, sets the cap. The agent stages it in the outbox; the human's click costs three seconds; the un-sendable email costs more.

tasks.text: Update each candidate's stage in the ATS after the debrief meeting
tasks.reasoning: An action on a person's process in the system of record. The agent may prepare the list of stage changes as an artifact, rung 1–2 work; the human executes in the ATS. If the volume makes that painful, the pain is information about the process, not a case for permissions.

tasks.text: Compile the weekly people-metrics table from the HRIS export
tasks.reasoning: Mechanical, checkable against the export, regenerable, feeding a human-owned narrative downstream. With a sampled error history, the least controversial climb on the board.

pattern: Rung 3 lives where work is mechanical, checkable, and undoable. The boundary crossings (publish, send, touch a person's record) are where humans stand.
postscript: The two rigged items (the shared-folder save and the newsletter send) show the tell isn't how routine a step feels but what its undo costs.
